walkthroughs.body_html:
Galaxies & Cosmology — a core area of GCSE Astronomy.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Galaxies & Cosmology brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Galaxies & Cosmology.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What is the current best estimate for the age of the universe?
options: About 13.8 billion years.
Infinite.
About 6,000 years.
Telescopes distort star positions.

mcqs.q: How do astronomers determine the chemical composition of a distant star?
options: By sending probes to collect samples.
Infinite.
By measuring its colour with the naked eye.
By analysing absorption lines in its spectrum.

mcqs.q: What is the principle behind stellar parallax?
options: A nearby star appears to shift against background stars as Earth orbits the Sun.
Infinite.
Stars actually move position throughout the year.
Telescopes distort star positions.
